- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of forecast horizon).
- Forecast shows gradual upward trend, but true prices often dip sharply after initial peak or show mean-reversion behavior.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price spikes in history (e.g., 97.01 → 90.85), where model fails to anticipate sharp downward correction.
- Model underestimates volatility in late forecast period (last 10 days), particularly when true prices show upward momentum or sudden recovery.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 2–5 days, especially in downward corrections.
- Model assumes linear continuation of recent trend, ignoring structural breaks or seasonal patterns.
- When true price drops below 85, model often fails to adjust downward, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model tends to overfit recent high prices, underestimating the probability of sharp corrections or mean reversion.
